Berate

bih-RATE · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To berate to scold someone angrily and at length.

The manager berated the new employee in front of the entire staff.

Worked Example

The furious coach berated the referee for nearly five minutes after the missed call.

A long, loud, angry scolding -- not a single sharp word -- is exactly what berate describes.

How Strong Is It? — scold → berate → excoriate

scold vs. berate

scold vs. berate: To scold is a general, everyday act of expressing anger at someone; to berate is a longer, angrier, more relentless version of the same thing.

excoriate vs. berate

excoriate vs. berate: Excoriate goes even further than berate, implying an almost merciless, scathing verbal attack.

Put it together

Put it together: be- ('thoroughly') + rate (an old verb meaning 'to scold') together give the long, thorough scolding berate describes.

Use the root in a new word: rate
